package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of a coordinated spam and phishing campaign. They are designed to lure users with promises of free resources or cheats, and direct them to phishing sites via links in their README.md files. The packages are mass-generated and serve no legitimate software purpose, instead acting as vehicles for social engineering and credential harvesting.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (user views README or package page)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package README (on npmjs.com or after install), the README displays a phishing link that entices the user to click, redirecting them to a phishing website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README.md files containing links to external, unrelated domains promising free resources or cheats are a common phishing tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages use README.md for documentation, not for promoting unrelated external sites or phishing campaigns.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to their own documentation or demo sites, but not to unrelated, suspicious domains.
key_indicators: README.md contains links to domains known for phishing
Links to domains not associated with the package author or project

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At attacker runtime, the script reads configuration and content files, generates random package names and descriptions, and prepares phishing links for inclusion in package files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated mass generation of packages with randomized names and phishing content is a hallmark of spam and phishing campaigns.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package creation is manual or semi-automated for legitimate projects, not for mass spam.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some organizations use automation for legitimate bulk publishing, but not for phishing.
key_indicators: Loops generating hundreds of packages per run
References to phishing domains in config

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At attacker runtime, the script programmatically publishes the generated package to npm, then verifies publication and logs the package URL for further use.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated publishing of thousands of packages is highly abnormal and indicative of spam or supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate publishing is typically manual or CI/CD-based for real projects, not for mass spam.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: CI/CD pipelines for legitimate package publishing.
key_indicators: Automated npm publish in a loop
No real code or functionality in the packages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At attacker runtime, the script logs into compromised or attacker-controlled WordPress sites and posts links to the malicious npm packages, boosting their SEO and visibility.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated posting of unrelated npm package links to news/blog sites is a classic SEO poisoning and spam tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate blog automation does not post unrelated package links for SEO manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated blog posting for legitimate content syndication.
key_indicators: Use of stolen or hardcoded credentials
Automated posting of package links to unrelated sites

attack_chain.action: Automated scripts generate thousands of spam npm packages with enticing names and phishing links in README.md.
Automated publishing of generated packages to npm using npm publish.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages become publicly available on npm.

attack_chain.action: Phishing links in README.md lure users to click, redirecting them to phishing or scam sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victims are exposed to phishing, credential harvesting, or referral scams.

attack_chain.action: Attacker posts links to the npm packages on unrelated news/blog sites to boost SEO and drive more traffic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased visibility and search ranking for malicious packages, amplifying victim exposure.

behavioral_signatures: README.md files containing links to unrelated external domains, especially those promising free resources or cheats
Mass publishing of packages with similar names/descriptions in a short time frame
Automated package creation and publishing scripts in package contents
file_indicators: Presence of automation scripts (e.g., generator.py, helper.txt) in package tarballs
network_indicators: Outbound links to domains such as legalcoins.vip, betapps.club, stumblegems.site, followersfree.store, etc.
Referral URLs to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress) with suspicious referral IDs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with README.md files containing links to known phishing or scam domains, especially those using social engineering language. Flag packages published in bulk with similar naming patterns or descriptions. Scan package tarballs for embedded automation scripts or evidence of mass generation. Track outbound links from package documentation to blocklisted or suspicious domains. Correlate with known phishing and SEO spam campaigns.
